artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
Steven Wilson's album 4½, released on January 22, 2016, is a progressive rock mini-album that serves as an interim release between his fourth solo album Hand. Cannot. Erase. and his subsequent full-length album To the Bone. The album compiles six tracks written during the recording sessions for Hand. Cannot. Erase. and The Raven That Refused to Sing (And Other Stories), featuring a blend of instrumental and vocal pieces that showcase Wilson's signature atmospheric and intricate soundscapes. Notably, the album includes a new version of "Don't Hate Me," originally a Porcupine Tree track, reimagined as a slower, more layered duet with Israeli singer Ninet Tayeb.

Musically, 4½ marks a return to more prominent guitar solos, which had been less emphasized on Wilson’s recent albums, adding a dynamic edge to the progressive rock foundation. The album’s production, handled by Wilson himself, maintains the high-quality, immersive experience typical of his work, with formats including CD, vinyl, and a Blu-ray edition featuring high-resolution stereo and 5.1 surround mixes. Critically, 4½ was well-received as a cohesive collection that bridges the gap between major releases, appreciated for its thoughtful composition and the emotional depth of its tracks, particularly the reinterpretation of "Don't Hate Me".
